H_hierarchical.evidence: The paper distinguishes AUTO and MANUAL operation, with manual OPEN/CLOSE/STOP commands, but it does not define an explicit parent-child state hierarchy.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Multiple threshold/event guards are present: water level reaches 4ft -> open, reaches 3ft -> close, and top/bottom limit switches stop motor motion.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Actions include driving open/close relays, stopping motor power through limit switches, LCD indication, GUI graphing, and buzzer/alarm output, but most are direct I/O commands.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The implemented controller has end-stop protection, but no explicit fault state, recovery transition, emergency stop, rollback, or from-any-state fault escape.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: Control semantics are split across hardware implementation, AUTO-mode software flowchart, Visual Basic manual panel description, and results discussion.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as manual mode and operator control imply takeover/priority rules over automatic operation that are not formalized as transitions.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions such as relay driving, LCD display, alarm output, GUI graphing, and limit-switch motor cutoff are described narratively rather than in a state/action table.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The guards are simple single-variable threshold or switch conditions; no explicit arithmetic or boolean-composed multi-variable guard is given.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite parent state with its own entry/during/exit behavior is specified.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: No from-any-state fault or recovery rule is declared.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no deep composite state or non-trivial initial pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The sample has threshold guards, but not arithmetic-plus-boolean guard formulas where SMT checking would be distinctively useful.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Continuous water-level display/graphing and end-stop cutoff are cross-cutting-ish behaviors, but they do not apply to three or more substates as an explicit global rule.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some outputs are abstractly described as recording usage and indicating/alarming people, although the implementation also commits to LCD, GUI, relay, and buzzer channels.

key_nl_quotes: Whenever the water level reaches the highest level (4ft) then the controller will open the gate.
The OPEN, CLOSE and STOP command is used for opening, closing and stopping the gate in manual mode.
one_line_pitch: A compact threshold-control stress case where guards, manual takeover behavior, relay actions, alarms, displays, and end-stop protection must be assembled from scattered hardware and software prose.
rationale: This is a meaningful EFSM benchmark because the modeler must recover threshold guards, manual-mode commands, actuator outputs, continuous indication, and limit-switch stopping behavior from non-adjacent paper sections. It directly stresses guard/action extraction and context integration, two known weak points of prior baselines. It is not a top candidate because hierarchy is only superficial and the paper lacks a true fault-recovery or global escape model.
